name: Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia, MacDermot Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia, MacDermot Type

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism with normal limb length
Radiological evidence of vertebral and epiphyseal dysplasia including flattened vertebral bodies and delayed ossification
Clinical or radiological signs of early-onset osteoarthritis predominantly affecting weight-bearing joints
Mild facial dysmorphic features including midface hypoplasia and flattened nasal bridge

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism plus radiological vertebral and epiphyseal abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always definitive due to limited data on causative mutations.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic growth pattern with normal limb length
Flattened vertebral bodies seen on spine imaging

searchTerms: delayed bone growth at growth plates

common.notes: Flattened nasal bridge and underdeveloped midface
searchTerms: mild flatness of cheeks and nose

common.notes: Reduced range of motion in affected joints

searchTerms: short height with normal brain function
short person with typical cognitive skills

occasional.notes: Abnormal development of the hip joint
Pain related to early degenerative changes

rare.notes: Potential cervical spine instability requiring monitoring

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications due to thoracic cage abnormalities
rare.notes: Restrictive lung disease secondary to skeletal deformities
searchTerms: lung issues due to rib cage

imaging: Radiographs showing platyspondyly and epiphyseal dysplasia
Delayed ossification centers in long bones
Possible hip dysplasia on pelvic X-rays
genetic: Mutations in COL2A1 gene suspected but not definitively established
other: Clinical assessment of disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism

distinguishingFeatures: More severe skeletal deformities at birth
Markedly shortened limbs in addition to trunk shortening
Higher incidence of ocular and hearing abnormalities
Disproportionate short-limb dwarfism rather than short trunk
Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing
FGFR3 gene mutation confirmed by genetic testing

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory insufficiency due to thoracic cage deformity
Atlantoaxial instability with risk of cervical myelopathy
references: MacDermot KD, et al. Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, MacDermot type: clinical and radiological features. J Med Genet. 1990.
Orphanet: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, MacDermot type. ORPHA:163668.
